mainTopic: The end of the עסיקין case; how three widows split a small estate (שמואל's waivers, the two-seizures approach, רבי נתן vs. רבי); partners in a shared fund
overview: The גמרא finishes a case about a buyer who finds people challenging the seller's ownership of his field (עסיקין). Without a guarantee, he may back out only until he takes possession by walking the boundaries. Some say that even with a guarantee he gets paid only once a court actually takes the field. A new משנה follows: three widows with כתובות of 100, 200 and 300 share an estate that is too small to pay them all. With 100 they split equally, with 200 they get 50/75/75, and with 300 they get 50/100/150. Business partners divide the same way. שמואל explains the uneven numbers through written waivers, in which a wife gives up her claim on the first hundred, and the גמרא tests that answer against the משנה's numbers. רב יעקב מנהר פקוד offers a different explanation: the money came in two separate batches. A ברייתא then says the משנה follows רבי נתן, while רבי holds that the wives divide equally. Finally the גמרא turns to the partners, and שמואל begins a case of two partners who invested 100 and 200; his ruling continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Without a guarantee, the buyer may back out only before taking possession
steps.stepSummary: If challengers (עסיקין) appear on a field sold without a guarantee, the buyer may cancel before taking possession but not after, because he knowingly bought a risky field.
steps.simpleTranslation: If people turn up who challenge the seller's ownership: before the buyer has taken possession, he can back out of the deal. Once he has taken possession, he cannot back out, because the seller can tell him: 'You knowingly accepted a sack full of knots, and you took it.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes a rule about a buyer who bought a field without a guarantee and then found people challenging the seller's ownership. It says when he may still cancel the deal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The dividing line is taking possession (חזקה). Before that, the buyer can still walk away. After that, the seller argues that a sale with no guarantee was a known gamble, so the buyer accepted the risk.

keyTerms.meaning: People who dispute the seller's ownership of the field, literally 'those who are busy with it'
To back out of the deal
A sack of knots, meaning a risky, uncertain package

phrases.english: disputants: as long as he has not taken possession of it,
phrases.notes: This sentence started on the previous page: ראובן sold a field to שמעון without a guarantee, and challengers showed up.

phrases.english: he can back out of the deal.
Once he has taken possession of it,
he cannot back out.
Because the seller can say to him:
You agreed to a sack of knots, and you took it.
phrases.notes: He means: you bought with no guarantee, so you knew you might be getting trouble.

steps.triggerLanguage: עַד שֶׁלֹּא הֶחְזִיק בָּהּ יָכוֹל לַחֲזוֹר בּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a ruling that began on the previous page
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In a sale without a guarantee, the buyer may cancel because of challengers only before he takes possession; after that he bears the risk he accepted.

steps.title: When does the buyer count as having taken possession?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks at what moment the buyer counts as having taken possession, since that moment decides whether he may still back out.
steps.simpleTranslation: And from when is he considered to have taken possession of it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a clarifying question about the rule it just gave. It sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 1 made everything depend on taking possession, so we need to know exactly when that happens. This is not an attack on the rule; it only defines its key term.

phrases.english: And from when does he take possession of it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the definition of the key term in step 1
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The exact moment the buyer counts as having taken possession

steps.title: Possession begins when he walks the boundaries
steps.stepSummary: The buyer counts as having taken possession once he treads along the field's boundaries.
steps.simpleTranslation: From when he walks along the boundaries of the field.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the buyer counts as having taken possession once he walks along the field's borders.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Walking the boundaries shows he is treating the field as his own. From that point he can no longer cancel because of challengers.

phrases.english: From when he treads on the boundaries.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Possession starts once he walks the field's boundaries.

steps.title: Second opinion: even with a guarantee he cannot demand his money right away
steps.stepSummary: Some say that even in a sale with a guarantee, the buyer cannot get a refund just because challengers appear; he must first actually lose the field in court.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: even when the field was sold with a guarantee, the rule is the same, because the seller can tell him: 'Show me your court document for collecting from me, and I will pay you.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second version of the rule (איכא דאמרי). It stretches the rule even to a sale that came with a guarantee.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A guarantee only promises payment if the buyer actually loses the field. Challengers alone have not taken anything yet. So the seller can say: once a court takes the field and gives you a collection document, I will pay.

keyTerms.meaning: A guarantee that the seller will pay back if the field is taken away
Your document for collecting (טירפא), showing the field was taken away

steps.whatToRemember: Without a guarantee, the buyer may back out only until he walks the boundaries. According to איכא דאמרי, even with a guarantee he gets paid only after a court has actually taken the field.

phrases.english: There are those who say:
Even when sold with a guarantee, it is also so.
phrases.notes: He means that even then, the buyer cannot demand a refund just because challengers appeared.

phrases.english: Because the seller can say to him:
Show me your collection document, and I will pay you.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A different version that extends step 1's rule to a sale with a guarantee
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even with a guarantee, the buyer cannot demand payment until a court has actually taken the field from him.

steps.title: New משנה: three widows and an estate of only one hundred
steps.stepSummary: A man dies with three wives whose כתובות are 100, 200 and 300. If the estate is only 100, they split it equally.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A man was married to three women and died. One wife's כתובה was one hundred, another's was two hundred, and another's was three hundred, and there is only one hundred in the estate. They divide it equally.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It describes three widows whose כתובות are different sizes and an estate too small to pay them all, and it rules on the first case: an estate of 100.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each wife's claim is at least 100, so each has an equal claim on the whole 100. That is why they split it equally, even though their כתובות differ.

keyTerms.meaning: The marriage contract, which promises the wife a sum when the marriage ends

steps.confusionAlert: Don't assume the split always matches the size of each כתובה. The numbers in the next cases follow a special pattern, and the גמרא ahead discusses them.

phrases.aramaic: מַתְנִי׳ מִי שֶׁהָיָה נָשׂוּי שָׁלֹשׁ נָשִׁים,
phrases.english: MISHNA: One who was married to three women
and died, and the כתובה of this one was one hundred,
and of this one two hundred,
and of this one three hundred,
and there is only one hundred there,
they divide equally.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי שֶׁהָיָה נָשׂוּי שָׁלֹשׁ נָשִׁים וָמֵת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה and a new topic
steps.mimraCoreRuling: With an estate of 100, the three widows split it equally.

steps.title: An estate of two hundred: 50, 75, 75
steps.stepSummary: With 200 in the estate, the wife of the 100 כתובה takes 50, and the wives of 200 and 300 each take three gold דינרים (75 each).
steps.simpleTranslation: If there were two hundred, the wife whose כתובה is one hundred takes fifty, and the wives of two hundred and three hundred take three gold דינרים each.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues with a second case: the estate is 200.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The wife of the 100 כתובה gets only 50, while the other two each get 75. So the split is not simply equal, and it is not in proportion to the כתובות either.

keyTerms.meaning: Of gold, referring to gold דינרים

phrases.english: If there were two hundred there,
the one of one hundred takes fifty,
those of two hundred and of three hundred
take three gold דינרים each.
phrases.notes: A gold דינר is worth 25 silver ones, so three gold equals 75.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The next case of the same משנה, with a larger estate

steps.title: An estate of three hundred: 50, 100, 150
steps.stepSummary: With 300 in the estate, the wives receive 50, 100 and six gold דינרים (150).
steps.simpleTranslation: If there were three hundred, the wife whose כתובה is one hundred takes fifty, the wife of two hundred takes one hundred, and the wife of three hundred takes six gold דינרים.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives its third case: the estate is 300.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here each wife gets exactly half of her כתובה: 50, 100, 150. Put the three cases side by side and you can see the shares change in an unusual way as the estate grows, which the גמרא will go on to examine.

keyTerms.meaning: Six gold דינרים, equal to 150 silver

steps.whatToRemember: Estate of 100: 33⅓ each. Estate of 200: 50, 75, 75. Estate of 300: 50, 100, 150.

phrases.english: If there were three hundred there,
the one of one hundred takes fifty,
and the one of two hundred takes one hundred,

phrases.aramaic: וְשֶׁל שְׁלֹשׁ מֵאוֹת שִׁשָּׁה שֶׁל זָהָב.
phrases.english: and the one of three hundred takes six gold דינרים.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The final case of the משנה's sequence

steps.title: Partners who invested into a shared fund
steps.stepSummary: The משנה ends by saying that three partners who put money into a shared fund split any loss or gain the same way.
steps.simpleTranslation: Similarly, three people who put money into a shared purse: whether they lost money or made a profit, this is how they divide it.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes its teaching by giving a business example that follows the same pattern as the three wives.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Three partners invested different amounts into one shared fund. When they split it up after a loss or a profit, each one's share follows how much they put in. The משנה is saying this kind of division also applies outside of כתובות.

keyTerms.meaning: put money into a shared purse (invested together)

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's way of dividing applies both to wives collecting כתובות and to partners in a shared business.

phrases.english: Similarly, three who put money into a purse,
whether they lost or made a profit
this is how they divide.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the משנה's estate-splitting cases to business partners.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Partners divide a loss or a profit according to the same principle used in the משנה.

steps.title: Why does the 100 wife get fifty?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the wife of the 100 כתובה gets 50 when the estate is 200, since she should only get a third of the first hundred.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: The wife of the hundred takes fifty? She only has a right to thirty-three and a third!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by attacking the משנה's number in the 200 case. It says the 100-wife seems to be getting too much.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 100-wife only has a claim on the first hundred, and all three wives have an equal claim on that hundred. So it should be split three ways, giving her 33⅓, not 50. The משנה's number seems wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: the Talmud's discussion of the משנה

phrases.english: GEMARA
The wife of the hundred takes fifty?
phrases.notes: This is the case from step 6, where the estate has 200.

phrases.english: Thirty-three and a third
is what she has!
phrases.notes: All three wives share the first hundred equally, so her part is one third of it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the number in the 200 estate case of the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that the 100-wife takes 50 when the estate is 200.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The first hundred belongs equally to all three wives, so each should get only 33⅓ of it.

steps.title: שמואל: the 200 wife waived the first hundred
steps.stepSummary: שמואל explains that the 200-wife wrote to the 100-wife that she gives up any claim to the first hundred.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: This is a case where the wife of the 200 wrote to the wife of the 100, "I have no legal claim or dealings with you regarding the hundred."
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל answers the question by describing a special situation the משנה must be talking about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the 200-wife gives up her share of the first hundred, only two wives claim it: the 100-wife and the 300-wife. Split two ways, each gets 50, which matches the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: "I have no legal claim or dealings with you" (a written waiver)

steps.confusionAlert: The 200-wife does not give up her כתובה. She only gives up her claim against the 100-wife on the first hundred.

phrases.english: Shmuel said:
When the wife of the 200 writes to the wife of the 100,
"I have no legal claim or dealings with you regarding the hundred."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: בְּכוֹתֶבֶת בַּעֲלַת מָאתַיִם לְבַעֲלַת מָנֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge by narrowing the case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case to a special situation (a written waiver)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: All three wives share the first hundred, so the 100-wife gets 33⅓.
steps.terutzMaskana: The 200-wife waived her claim to the first hundred, so it is split between two wives, 50 each.

steps.title: Then the 300 wife should get more
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges שמואל: if the 200-wife gave up the first hundred, the 300-wife should get more than the 200-wife, not the same 75.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, look at the latter part: the wives of 200 and 300 each take three gold דינרים. But the 300-wife can say to her, "You removed yourself from the first hundred!"
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests שמואל's answer against the next part of the same ruling and finds a problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה gives the 200-wife and the 300-wife the same amount (75 each). But if the 200-wife waived the first hundred, she should only share the second hundred. The 300-wife should then get 50 from each hundred, totaling 100, while the 200-wife gets only 50.

keyTerms.meaning: the latter part of the statement
of gold (a gold דינר equals 25 silver דינרים)

phrases.english: If so, say the latter part:
the wife of 200 and the wife of 300
take three gold [dinars] each.
phrases.notes: Three gold coins equal 75 silver ones, from step 6.

phrases.english: Let her say to her:
But you removed yourself from it!
phrases.notes: "It" is the first hundred, which she waived.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks שמואל's answer by showing it does not fit the second half of the 200 case.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's explanation that the 200-wife waived the first hundred.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If she waived the first hundred, the 300-wife should take more of it, so the two should not receive an equal 75 each.

steps.title: The 200-wife only stepped back from fighting the 100-wife
steps.stepSummary: The 200-wife can say she only gave up arguing with the 100-wife. Against the 300-wife she still claims the first hundred, so the two of them split the rest equally at 75 each.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because she can say to her: I only removed myself from legal dealings and involvement.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from Step 11. The 200-wife's waiver only applies to the 100-wife, so against the 300-wife she keeps her full claim.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 11 assumed the 200-wife gave up the first hundred completely, which should have given the 300-wife more. Here the גמרא says her waiver was narrow: she only agreed not to go to court against the 100-wife. Against the 300-wife she still claims the first hundred, so the two of them have equal claims to the remaining 150 and each takes 75.

keyTerms.meaning: Legal dealings and involvement, meaning a court claim or dispute
I removed myself, meaning I stepped back

steps.confusionAlert: The waiver is not a full giving-up of money. It only works against the person it was written to (the 100-wife), not against the 300-wife.

phrases.english: Because she can say to her:
From legal dealings and involvement
is all that I removed myself from.
phrases.notes: She means: I only stopped fighting the 100-wife. I never gave my rights to you.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 11 and defends שמואל's explanation.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the scope of the waiver
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The 200-wife fully gave up the first hundred, so the 300-wife should get more than her.
steps.terutzMaskana: The waiver only covers disputes with the 100-wife. Against the 300-wife, the 200-wife still claims the first hundred, so they split the remaining 150 evenly.

steps.title: Why does the 200-wife get 100 when the estate is 300?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's 300 case and asks why the 200-wife gets 100. By שמואל's logic she should get only 75.
steps.simpleTranslation: If there were three hundred there, etc. The one of two hundred gets a hundred? She should only have seventy-five!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now turns to the משנה's case of a 300 estate. It asks why the 200-wife gets a full 100.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under שמואל's setup, the 200-wife has given up the first hundred to the 100-wife. She also has no claim at all on the third hundred, since her כתובה is only 200. That leaves her claiming only 150 of what remains, shared with the 300-wife, so she should get half: 75, not 100.

keyTerms.meaning: Etc., meaning the rest of the quoted line in the משנה

phrases.english: If there were three hundred there, etc.
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה from Step 7, where the shares were 50, 100 and 150.

phrases.english: The one of two hundred gets a hundred?
She should only have seventy-five!

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁל מָאתַיִם מָנֶה? שִׁבְעִים וַחֲמִשָּׁה הוּא דְּאִית לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies שמואל's waiver idea to the next case in the משנה (300 estate) and finds a problem.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that the 200-wife receives 100 when the estate is 300.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the 200-wife gave up the first hundred and has no claim on the third hundred, she claims only 150 against the 300-wife. That gives her half, which is 75, not 100.

steps.title: The 300-wife also wrote a waiver on the first hundred
steps.stepSummary: שמואל explains that in the 300 case, the 300-wife wrote to both other wives that she has no claim on the first hundred. This produces 50, 100 and 150.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: It is where the woman of three hundred writes to the woman of two hundred and to the woman of one hundred: 'I have no legal dealings with you regarding the hundred.'
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל answers the question from Step 13. He describes another written waiver, this time from the 300-wife.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 300-wife steps out of the first hundred, so the 100-wife and the 200-wife split it, 50 each. The second hundred is split by the 200-wife and the 300-wife, 50 each, which brings the 200-wife to 100. The third hundred belongs only to the 300-wife, so she ends with 150.

keyTerms.meaning: The owner of, meaning the wife holding a כתובה of that amount

steps.whatToRemember: שמואל explains the משנה's numbers through written waivers. With 200 in the estate, the 200-wife waived toward the 100-wife only, giving 50, 75 and 75. With 300, the 300-wife also waived the first hundred toward both, giving 50, 100 and 150.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the משנה's odd-looking splits are not a general math rule. Each one comes from a specific agreement the wives made.

phrases.english: שמואל said:
It is where the woman of three hundred writes
to the woman of two hundred and to the woman of one hundred:
'I have no legal dealings with you regarding the hundred.'
phrases.notes: "The hundred" means the first hundred of the estate.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: בְּכוֹתֶבֶת בַּעֲלַת שְׁלֹשׁ מֵאוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 13 by describing an extra waiver.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defining the case through an added written agreement
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only the 200-wife waived, so she should get 75.
steps.terutzMaskana: The 300-wife waived the first hundred toward both other wives. The shares are 50 for the 100-wife, 50+50=100 for the 200-wife, and 50+100=150 for the 300-wife.

steps.title: A new approach: the money came in two batches
steps.stepSummary: רב יעקב מנהר פקוד, quoting רבינא, says that both the רישא and the סיפא of the משנה are cases of two separate seizures of money.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יעקב מנהר פקוד said in the name of רבינא: The first part of the משנה is about two seizures, and the last part is also about two seizures.
steps.whatsHappening: A new אמורא gives a fresh way to explain the strange numbers in the משנה, without needing any wife to give up her claim. He sets out the idea here, and the next steps show the math.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל needed a written waiver to explain the numbers, and that led to many challenges. רב יעקב says the estate was not collected all at once. It came in two separate batches, and the wives divided each batch on its own. That is why the totals come out uneven.

keyTerms.meaning: The first part (clause) of the משנה
The last part (clause) of the משנה
Seizures, the times the wives took hold of money from the estate

steps.confusionAlert: This is not another answer for שמואל. It is a totally separate explanation that replaces the idea of one wife writing a waiver to the others.

phrases.english: Rav Ya'akov of Nehar Pekod
said in the name of Ravina:
The first clause is with two seizures,
and the latter clause is with two seizures.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב יַעֲקֹב מִנְּהַר פְּקוֹד מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרָבִינָא אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves שמואל's waiver approach behind and offers a different setup that explains the משנה's numbers.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case: the money arrived in two separate collections
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The numbers seemed to need one wife to give up part of her claim, as שמואל said.
steps.terutzMaskana: No waiver is needed. Dividing two separate batches, one after the other, produces the משנה's numbers.

steps.title: The math for the 200 case: 75 then 125
steps.stepSummary: In the רישא, 75 came in first and 125 came in later, which gives totals of 50, 75 and 75.
steps.simpleTranslation: The first clause has two seizures: seventy-five fell in at one time, and one hundred twenty-five fell in at another time.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows how the two-batch idea explains the first case of the משנה, where the estate totals 200.
steps.deeperAnalysis: First batch (75): all three wives claim it, so each gets 25. Second batch (125): the 100-wife can claim only 75 more, so that 75 is split three ways at 25 each, and she ends with 50. The last 50 is split between the other two at 25 each, so they end with 75 each, just as the משנה says.

keyTerms.meaning: Fell in, meaning became available to collect
At one time, in one batch

phrases.english: The first clause is with two seizures —
where seventy-five fell in at one time,
and one hundred twenty-five at another time.

steps.triggerLanguage: רֵישָׁא בִּשְׁתֵּי תְפִיסוֹת דְּנָפְלוּ שִׁבְעִין וַחֲמִשָּׁה בְּחַד זִימְנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the first half of רב יעקב's statement with actual numbers.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Working through the case with numbers
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It was unclear how 200 could come out as 50, 75 and 75.
steps.terutzMaskana: Two batches of 75 and 125, each divided by itself, give exactly 50, 75 and 75.

steps.title: The math for the 300 case: 75 then 225
steps.stepSummary: In the סיפא, 75 came in first and 225 came in later, which gives totals of 50, 100 and 150.
steps.simpleTranslation: The last clause has two seizures: seventy-five fell in at one time, and two hundred twenty-five fell in at another time.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא applies the same two-batch idea to the משנה's case where the estate totals 300.
steps.deeperAnalysis: First batch (75): each wife gets 25. Second batch (225): the first 75 is split three ways, so the 100-wife ends with 50. The next 100 is claimed only by the 200-wife and the 300-wife, so they split it 50 each, and the 200-wife ends with 100. The last 50 belongs only to the 300-wife, so she ends with 150.
steps.whatToRemember: The two-seizure approach explains both cases of the משנה with no waiver at all: (75 then 125) gives 50/75/75, and (75 then 225) gives 50/100/150.

phrases.english: The latter clause is with two seizures —
where seventy-five fell in at one time,
and two hundred twenty-five at another time.

steps.triggerLanguage: סֵיפָא בִּשְׁתֵּי תְפִיסוֹת דְּנָפְלוּ שִׁבְעִים וַחֲמִשָּׁה בְּחַד זִימְנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes רב יעקב's explanation by applying it to the second case of the משנה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Working through the case with numbers
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שמואל needed the 300-wife to waive her claim to explain 50/100/150.
steps.terutzMaskana: Two batches of 75 and 225 give 50/100/150 on their own.

steps.title: The משנה follows רבי נתן, but רבי says divide equally
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says the משנה's method of division is רבי נתן's view. רבי disagrees and rules that the wives split the estate equally.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא: This is the teaching of רבי נתן. רבי says: I do not agree with רבי נתן's words in these cases. Rather, they divide equally.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא that tells us whose opinion the משנה follows, and that another תנא disagrees.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The uneven division in the משנה is only one view, that of רבי נתן. רבי (רבי יהודה הנשיא) holds that each wife simply gets an equal share of the estate. Because of this, all the explanations above are explanations of רבי נתן's view only.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's uneven division (50/75/75 and 50/100/150) is רבי נתן's view. רבי holds the wives divide the estate equally.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the whole complicated calculation is a dispute among תנאים, not an agreed rule.

phrases.english: It was taught: This is the teaching of Rabbi Natan.
phrases.notes: 'This' means the way our משנה divides the money among the three wives.

phrases.english: Rabbi says:
phrases.notes: 'רבי' with no other name means רבי יהודה הנשיא.

phrases.aramaic: אֵין אֲנִי רוֹאֶה דְּבָרָיו שֶׁל רַבִּי נָתָן בְּאֵלּוּ,
phrases.english: I do not see Rabbi Natan's words in these cases,
rather, they divide equally.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Steps back from the math to say whose opinion the משנה follows, and brings a disagreeing view.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה's division follows רבי נתן. רבי holds the wives divide the estate equally.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה about three partners
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה: three people who put money into a shared purse divide the same way as the wives.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'And so too, three people who deposited money.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is quoting a new line from the משנה so it can discuss it. This is a setup line that prepares for שמואל's statement in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the סוגיא dealt with three wives sharing one estate. The משנה applies the same kind of split to business partners who invested different amounts. The גמרא now turns from the wives to the partners.

keyTerms.meaning: And so too: the same rule applies here
Who deposited or threw in money, meaning they invested together

phrases.english: And so too, three who deposited.
phrases.notes: These are the opening words of the משנה's line. The full line adds 'into a purse,' meaning a shared business fund.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the wives' case, which ended with the ברייתא about רבי נתן and רבי, to the משנה's next case about business partners.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Partners who invested different amounts divide in a way similar to the wives in the משנה.

steps.title: שמואל begins: two partners, 100 and 200
steps.stepSummary: שמואל describes two partners who put money into a shared purse, one investing 100 and the other 200. His ruling comes next.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: If two people put money into a purse, one put in a hundred and the other two hundred...
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל is setting up a case about two partners who invested unequal amounts. The sentence breaks off here, and his ruling continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל picks a simpler case than the משנה's three partners: only two people, with one investing twice as much as the other. This case sets up the question of how profits are split when the investments are unequal.

keyTerms.meaning: A purse, meaning a shared business fund
A unit of money equal to one hundred זוז

steps.confusionAlert: The sentence is not finished yet. Don't try to work out שמואל's ruling from these words alone, because it comes on the next amud.

phrases.english: Shmuel said: Two who deposited into a purse,
this one a hundred and that one two hundred —

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the explanation of the משנה line quoted in step 19, using a simpler two-partner case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sets up the case of two partners who invested 100 and 200. The ruling follows on the next amud.
